name: Thor, Thunder Guardian
loreTies: Thor embodies thunder guardianship, strength, storm protection, and oath defense within The Storm-Rooted Aesir Holds.
The Thunder-Oath Gate allows this deity to enter Ascension-era dungeon routes without collapsing the individuality of other Realms.
Asgardian culture, symbols, weapons, and divine law shape every ability, artifact, silhouette, and combat choice.
shortBackstory: Thor, Thunder Guardian, is a playable god in Mythos Gates: Ascension. Thor is the true source-realm divinity behind the mythology — thunder guardianship, strength, storm protection, and oath defense. Ascension expands divine power during the current Gate crisis; it does not turn a mortal into a god.

chapters.title: Divine Origin
chapters.text: Thor is not a mortal hero inspired by myth. Thor is the actual god recognized by Asgardian source culture, born from the supernatural laws of The Storm-Rooted Aesir Holds. Their domain — thunder guardianship, strength, storm protection, and oath defense — determines their symbols, weapons, posture, combat instincts, and relationship to sacred authority.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Within Asgardian, Thor expresses the civilization rather than merely representing it. Their visual identity must carry the materials, beauty standards, divine symbols, and sacred rules of The Storm-Rooted Aesir Holds. Their gameplay role, Guardian, must grow from mythology first and mechanics second.

chapters.title: Mythos Gate Wound
chapters.text: During the Ascension era, Thor can interact with The Thunder-Oath Gate because divine beings are intrinsically connected to their Realms. The Gate does not become a simple teleportation portal; it is a mysterious boundary where separate mythological realities become traversable. Thor understands some rites of crossing, but not the complete origin of the Mythos Gates.

chapters.title: Dungeon Role
chapters.text: When selected by the player, Thor enters the dungeon alone as one god or goddess against multiple enemies. No army follows. No squad shares control. Every room, trap, shrine, relic, elite, and boss encounter must test how thunder guardianship, strength, storm protection, and oath defense survives pressure from creatures, rival Realm laws, and unstable Gate conditions.

chapters.title: Ascension Conflict
chapters.text: Ascension is the current story arc, not the permanent end-state of the Mythos Gates universe. For Thor, Ascension means restoration, awakening, evolution, or expansion of existing divine power. Their personal conflict is to recover strength without reducing Asgardian mythology into raw fuel for the crisis.

relationshipHooks: Faction witnesses interpret how Thor crosses The Thunder-Oath Gate.
Rival deities challenge the limits of cross-Realm travel.
Dungeon lore pickups reveal Gate mystery without resolving the full origin.
developmentStatus: Playable deity backstory aligned to Mythos Gates identity, one-deity dungeon runs, current Ascension arc, and preserved Lore Codex canon.
mythicSource: source culture humans later copied as Norse myth
visualCanon: Hrodda is an oath-witness shaped by Valkyrie law and skald memory. Her staff, storm-lit eye scar, iron-gray braids, and oath-ring cloak plates should feel like the origin of later human saga judges, not a Viking costume.
title: Thunder Guardian

mythosGatesCanon.identityRule: Thor is the actual god of Asgardian source mythology, never a mortal hero or generic champion.
mythosGatesCanon.arcRule: Ascension restores, awakens, evolves, or expands existing divine power; it does not make the character a god for the first time.
mythosGatesCanon.mysteryRule: The backstory may reveal how this deity interacts with the Mythos Gates, but must not resolve the full origin of the Gates.
